key_insight: This paper argues that robot policies should not start learning motion from scratch. By learning reusable action priors, the model can transfer motion knowledge across different robot bodies and improve cross-embodiment manipulation.
problem_solved: Existing VLA models inherit strong visual and language understanding from a VLM backbone, but their action modules must still learn physical control and temporal motion dynamics with little prior knowledge. This makes training inefficient and hurts performance, especially when transferring to robots with different embodiments.
method: Learn action priors that capture reusable motion patterns before full policy learning.
Use these priors to guide the action module so it does not need to discover temporal dynamics and cross-modal alignment simultaneously.
Design the policy for cross-embodiment manipulation, enabling transfer across robots with different kinematics and body structures.
impact: For practitioners, this can reduce data and training burden when building robot manipulation policies. It also improves the chance that a policy trained on one robot can generalize to another, making VLA systems more practical for real-world deployment.

paper_title: Learning Action Priors for Cross-embodiment Robot Manipulation
paper_authors: Dong Jing, Tianqi Zhang, Jiaqi Liu, Jinman Zhao, Zelong Sun
